name: Chat Settings
summary: Where a user turns auto-delete off, and where they delete every chat or every memory at once.
overview: Chat Settings is two switches and two doors. The switch decides how long chats live: sixty days with it on, 550 days with it off. Off is not "keep forever". The doors delete everything — all previous chats, or all memories — and neither can be undone.

It is reached through the side panel, which gains a fourth destination to carry it. That route is the reason this is a feature rather than a screen: nothing else in the product deletes at this scale, and the only thing standing between a user and an empty history is one dialog.

The file draws the surface two ways — on the gradient, and with the auto-delete row on a card. They disagree about the page title as well as the surface, so both are documented rather than one being picked.

states.name: The panel, with Settings
states.description: The side panel gains a fourth destination under Memory. This is the only route to the settings page that the file draws.

states.name: Settings
states.description: Auto-delete on, and both delete actions live. Two content states: the toggle on and off, the second carrying the toast that confirms it.

states.name: Confirming a delete
states.description: The dialog, its typed confirmation, and the keyboard it makes room for. Three content states: at rest, with the keyboard up and Delete still held back, and with the word typed and Delete live.

states.name: Both deletes spent
states.description: After both have run. The rows stay in place and go quiet rather than disappearing, so the setting is still legible as something that exists.

behaviour.rule: Auto-delete sets the window, it does not remove it
behaviour.detail: On by default and sixty days. Turning it off does not keep chats indefinitely — it moves them to 550 days, after which they are deleted anyway. Both numbers are stated in days rather than as a span, so the number a user reads is the number the system holds. What happens to memories saved from an expired chat is covered by the delete-chats dialog, which says they survive.
Turning it off raises “Auto-delete for chats disabled” at the top of the screen with a dismiss control. The file draws the disabled toast; the enabled one is its mirror.

behaviour.rule: Deleting is gated on typing the word
behaviour.detail: Both dialogs ask the user to type Delete, and hold the Delete button in a held-back red until they do. Neither dialog can be satisfied by tapping alone.
Deleting chats leaves memories, and the dialog says so. Deleting memories leaves chat history, and that dialog says so too. Each row is spent on its own.

behaviour.rule: A spent row stays and dims
behaviour.detail: The last frame keeps both rows in place at reduced opacity rather than removing them. Whether they recover — and when — is not drawn.
The delete rows sit directly under the setting with no intermediate step. The dialog is the only gate, and the only place the consequence is written down.
